title: kstrail's spontaneous swimmers are matched by a Laplacian-only twin: taxis is not necessary for S+I+M
summary: I replaced kstrail's taxis flux by a local mass-conserving reaction rho(1-rho)(c_a a - c_h h - ref), keeping all fields, rates and the volume-filling factor, with the converted mass redistributed over a screened-Poisson range Lm=5. From the same noise the twin forms 8-17 discrete unsaturated bodies of kstrail's size, and 10/10 of the most persistent tracks travel >=5 body lengths on 3/3 seeds (9/10 at dt/2), against 10/10 in kstrail. Removing the slow inhibitor (fh=0) gives static coarsening spots, as chi_h=0 does in kstrail. Motility of trail swimmers is therefore not beyond diffusion; what differs is the twin's need for a redistribution range (a global constraint collapses it to one domain-scale swimmer), faster bodies (0.8 vs 0.5) and a slower, different formation route.

finding.operator: self-repellent trail taxis (Keller-Segel flux -div(rho(1-rho)(chi_a grad a - chi_h grad h)))
finding.control: matched Laplacian-only twin (taxis replaced by local reaction with screened-Poisson mass redistribution, Lm=5, fa=0.1, fh=0.25); its own fh=0 ablation; global-mean variant
finding.result: twin: top-10 tracks >=5 BL 10/10/10 on seeds 0-2 (median 7.0-7.5 BL, max speed 0.80-0.84, 8-10 bodies at t=600), 9/10 at dt/2; kstrail: 10/10/10 (median 8.0-10.2 BL, 0.46-0.61, 9-11 bodies); twin fh=0: 0/0 (median 0.4 BL); global-mean twin: a single domain-scale swimmer
